category: Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox > Regression & Model Fitting
description: Linear, generalized linear, nonlinear, mixed-effects, regularized and machine-learning regression models, plus the diagnostic and inference methods that go with them.

tools.name: fitlm
tools.description: Fit a linear regression model by least squares and return a LinearModel object containing coefficients, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, R-squared and an ANOVA table. It accepts matrices or a table plus a Wilkinson formula, and handles categorical predictors automatically. Displaying the returned object prints a full regression summary.
tools.usage:
mdl = fitlm(tbl)
mdl = fitlm(tbl, modelspec)
mdl = fitlm(X, y)
mdl = fitlm(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: modelspec
parameters.description: 'linear', 'interactions', 'purequadratic', 'quadratic', 'polyIJK', or a formula like 'y ~ x1 + x2 + x1:x2'.

parameters.name: 'CategoricalVars'
parameters.description: Which predictors to treat as categorical.

parameters.name: 'RobustOpts'
parameters.description: 'on' or a weight function name for robust (M-estimator) fitting.

parameters.name: 'Weights'
parameters.description: Observation weights for weighted least squares.

parameters.name: 'Intercept'
parameters.description: Logical; set false to fit through the origin.

tools.notes: Access results through mdl.Coefficients, mdl.Residuals, mdl.Fitted and anova(mdl). Use predict(mdl, newTbl) for new data.

tools.name: fitglm
tools.description: Fit a generalized linear model with a specified error distribution and link function, covering logistic, Poisson, gamma and probit regression. It returns a GeneralizedLinearModel object with the same inspection and prediction interface as fitlm. Use it whenever the response is binary, a count, or otherwise non-normal.
tools.usage:
mdl = fitglm(tbl)
mdl = fitglm(X, y, modelspec, Name, Value)
mdl = fitglm(tbl, modelspec, 'Distribution', dist)

parameters.name: 'BinomialSize'
parameters.description: Number of trials per observation for binomial responses.

parameters.name: 'Offset'
parameters.description: Known additive term on the linear predictor scale, e.g. log exposure for Poisson rates.

tools.name: fitnlm
tools.description: Fit a nonlinear regression model defined by a model function handle and initial parameter estimates. It returns a NonLinearModel object with parameter estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals and residual diagnostics. Use it for mechanistic models such as exponential decay, Michaelis-Menten or logistic growth.
tools.usage:
mdl = fitnlm(X, y, modelfun, beta0)
mdl = fitnlm(tbl, modelfun, beta0)
mdl = fitnlm(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: modelfun
parameters.description: Function handle @(b, X) that returns the predicted response.

parameters.name: beta0
parameters.description: Initial parameter values; a poor guess can prevent convergence.

parameters.name: 'Weights'
parameters.description: Observation weights or a weight function handle.

parameters.name: 'Options'
parameters.description: statset structure controlling tolerances and iteration limits.

tools.notes: Scale parameters to similar magnitudes and try several starting points if the fit fails to converge.

tools.name: stepwiselm
tools.description: Build a linear regression model by stepwise term selection, adding and removing terms according to p-value or criterion thresholds. You specify the starting model and the upper bound of terms that may be entered. Use it for exploratory model building, but be aware that stepwise selection inflates apparent significance.
tools.usage:
mdl = stepwiselm(tbl)
mdl = stepwiselm(X, y)
mdl = stepwiselm(___, modelspec, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'PEnter' / 'PRemove'
parameters.description: p-value thresholds for adding and removing terms.

parameters.name: 'Verbose'
parameters.description: 0, 1 or 2 to control the step-by-step report.

tools.notes: Prefer lasso or cross-validated model comparison when you need honest inference.

tools.name: stepwiseglm
tools.description: Stepwise term selection for generalized linear models, combining fitglm's distribution/link options with automatic term entry and removal. Criteria include deviance, AIC and BIC. Use it for logistic or Poisson models where the relevant predictor set is not known in advance.
tools.usage:
mdl = stepwiseglm(tbl)
mdl = stepwiseglm(X, y, modelspec, Name, Value)

tools.name: fitlme
tools.description: Fit a linear mixed-effects model with both fixed and random effects, specified by a formula with grouping terms in parentheses. It is the right tool for repeated-measures, longitudinal and hierarchical data where observations within a group are correlated. Returns a LinearMixedModel with fixed-effect estimates, random-effect predictions and covariance parameters.
tools.usage:
lme = fitlme(tbl, formula)
lme = fitlme(tbl, formula, Name, Value)

parameters.name: formula
parameters.description: Wilkinson notation with random terms, e.g. 'y ~ 1 + x + (1 + x | group)'.

tools.notes: fitglme extends this to non-normal responses. Compare nested models with compare(lme1, lme2).

tools.name: regress
tools.description: Perform multiple linear regression using least squares, returning coefficients, confidence intervals, residuals and regression statistics. It is a lower-level alternative to fitlm that works purely on matrices and requires you to add the intercept column yourself. Use it when you want a lightweight numeric result rather than a model object.
tools.usage:
b = regress(y, X)
[b, bint] = regress(y, X)
[b, bint, r, rint, stats] = regress(y, X, alpha)

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Design matrix; include a column of ones for an intercept.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Significance level for the confidence intervals (default 0.05).

tools.notes: Forgetting the intercept column is the most common mistake. fitlm adds it automatically.

tools.name: robustfit
tools.description: Fit a linear model by iteratively reweighted least squares with a robust weight function, which greatly reduces the influence of outliers. Bisquare weighting is the default and works well for contaminated data. Returns coefficients and a stats structure with robust standard errors.
tools.usage:
b = robustfit(X, y)
b = robustfit(X, y, wfun, tune, const)
[b, stats] = robustfit(___)

parameters.name: tune
parameters.description: Tuning constant for the weight function.

tools.notes: fitlm(..., 'RobustOpts', 'on') gives the same fit inside a full LinearModel object.

tools.name: nlinfit
tools.description: Estimate nonlinear model coefficients by iterative least squares (Levenberg-Marquardt), returning the coefficients, residuals, Jacobian and error covariance. Unlike fitnlm it returns raw numeric outputs designed to feed nlparci and nlpredci. Supports weighted fitting and several error models.
tools.usage:
beta = nlinfit(X, Y, modelfun, beta0)
[beta, R, J, CovB, MSE] = nlinfit(___)
[___] = nlinfit(___, options, Name, Value)

parameters.name: modelfun
parameters.description: Function handle @(b, X) returning predicted values.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: statset options controlling TolFun, TolX, MaxIter, RobustWgtFun.

parameters.name: 'Weights'
parameters.description: Observation weights or a weight function.

tools.name: nlparci
tools.description: Compute confidence intervals for nonlinear model parameters from the residuals and Jacobian (or covariance matrix) returned by nlinfit. It uses the asymptotic normal approximation with a t-distribution correction. Use it to report uncertainty on fitted physical parameters.
tools.usage:
ci = nlparci(beta, resid, 'jacobian', J)
ci = nlparci(beta, resid, 'covar', CovB)
ci = nlparci(___, 'alpha', alpha)

parameters.name: 'jacobian' / 'covar'
parameters.description: Jacobian matrix or estimated coefficient covariance.

tools.name: nlpredci
tools.description: Compute predicted values with confidence or prediction intervals for a nonlinear regression model. The 'PredOpt' option switches between a confidence interval for the mean response and a prediction interval for a new observation. Use it to draw uncertainty bands around a nonlinear fit.
tools.usage:
[Ypred, delta] = nlpredci(modelfun, X, beta, R, 'Jacobian', J)
[Ypred, delta] = nlpredci(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: modelfun
parameters.description: The same model function handle used to fit.

parameters.name: 'Jacobian' / 'Covar'
parameters.description: Jacobian or coefficient covariance from nlinfit.

tools.name: lasso
tools.description: Fit lasso or elastic-net regularized linear regression over a sequence of regularization strengths, driving unimportant coefficients exactly to zero. With cross-validation it returns the lambda that minimizes MSE and the more parsimonious one-standard-error choice. Use it for variable selection with many correlated predictors.
tools.usage:
B = lasso(X, y)
[B, FitInfo] = lasso(X, y, Name, Value)
[B, FitInfo] = lasso(X, y, 'CV', k)

parameters.name: 'Alpha'
parameters.description: 1 (default) for pure lasso, values in (0,1) for elastic net, near 0 approaches ridge.

parameters.name: 'CV'
parameters.description: Number of cross-validation folds, or a cvpartition object.

parameters.name: 'Lambda'
parameters.description: Explicit regularization values; otherwise a geometric sequence is generated.

tools.name: ridge
tools.description: Fit ridge regression coefficients for one or more ridge parameters, shrinking coefficients toward zero to stabilize estimates under multicollinearity. Unlike lasso it never sets coefficients exactly to zero. The scaled flag controls whether coefficients are returned on the standardized or original data scale.
tools.usage:
B = ridge(y, X, k)
B = ridge(y, X, k, scaled)

parameters.name: scaled
parameters.description: 1 (default) returns coefficients for standardized data; 0 restores the original scale and adds an intercept.

tools.notes: With scaled = 0 the first row of B is the intercept.

tools.name: plsregress
tools.description: Partial least squares regression, which projects predictors onto latent components chosen to maximize covariance with the response. It handles many highly collinear predictors and more predictors than observations, which is why it dominates chemometrics and spectroscopy. Returns loadings, scores, regression coefficients and explained variance.
tools.usage:
[XL, YL] = plsregress(X, Y, ncomp)
[XL, YL, XS, YS, BETA, PCTVAR, MSE, stats] = plsregress(X, Y, ncomp)
[___] = plsregress(___, 'CV', k)

parameters.name: ncomp
parameters.description: Number of PLS components to compute.

parameters.name: 'CV'
parameters.description: Folds (or cvpartition) for cross-validated MSE estimation.

parameters.name: 'MCReps'
parameters.description: Monte Carlo repetitions of the cross-validation.

tools.name: mvregress
tools.description: Fit a multivariate linear regression model where each observation has several correlated responses, estimating both the regression coefficients and the response covariance matrix. It supports missing responses via an EM algorithm. Use it for seemingly unrelated regressions and repeated-measures data with a common design.
tools.usage:
beta = mvregress(X, Y)
[beta, Sigma, E, CovB, logL] = mvregress(X, Y, Name, Value)

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Design matrix, or a cell array of per-observation design matrices.

tools.name: mnrfit
tools.description: Fit a multinomial logistic regression model for a nominal or ordinal categorical response with more than two levels. It returns coefficient estimates, deviance and per-coefficient statistics, and mnrval computes predicted category probabilities. Use it when a logistic model must choose among several classes.
tools.usage:
B = mnrfit(X, Y)
[B, dev, stats] = mnrfit(X, Y, Name, Value)

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: Categorical response: a column of category indices, a categorical array, or a matrix of counts.

tools.notes: In newer releases fitmnr provides an object-based interface with the same modelling capability.

tools.name: fitrlinear
tools.description: Fit a linear regression model to high-dimensional data using SGD, ASGD, dual SGD or LBFGS solvers with lasso or ridge regularization. It scales to millions of predictors and observations where fitlm would be infeasible. Supports automatic cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitrlinear(X, Y)
Mdl = fitrlinear(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
[Mdl, FitInfo, HyperparameterOptimizationResults] = fitrlinear(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'ObservationsIn'
parameters.description: 'rows' (default) or 'columns'; column orientation is faster for wide data.

tools.name: fitrsvm
tools.description: Train a support vector machine regression model with linear, Gaussian or polynomial kernels. The epsilon-insensitive loss makes it robust to small errors and the box constraint controls the tolerance for larger ones. Best suited to small and medium datasets with nonlinear relationships.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitrsvm(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitrsvm(X, Y)
Mdl = fitrsvm(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'KernelScale'
parameters.description: Scale factor, or 'auto' for a heuristic.

parameters.name: 'Epsilon'
parameters.description: Width of the insensitive tube around the fit.

parameters.name: 'Standardize'
parameters.description: Logical; strongly recommended for RBF kernels.

parameters.name: 'OptimizeHyperparameters'
parameters.description: 'auto' or a cell of parameter names for Bayesian optimization.

tools.name: fitrtree
tools.description: Grow a binary regression decision tree that predicts a continuous response by recursive splitting. Trees are interpretable, handle mixed data types and missing values with surrogate splits, and need no feature scaling. Prune with the cost-complexity level or limit MinLeafSize to control overfitting.
tools.usage:
tree = fitrtree(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
tree = fitrtree(X, Y)
tree = fitrtree(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'MinLeafSize'
parameters.description: Minimum observations per leaf (default 1); increasing it regularizes the tree.

parameters.name: 'MaxNumSplits'
parameters.description: Maximum number of branch node splits.

parameters.name: 'Surrogate'
parameters.description: 'off' (default) or 'on' to handle missing predictor values.

tools.name: fitrensemble
tools.description: Train an ensemble of regression learners using LSBoost gradient boosting or bagging. Ensembles of shallow trees typically deliver the best accuracy of any off-the-shelf tabular regression method. Key hyperparameters are the number of learners, the learning rate and the tree depth.
tools.usage:
Mdl = fitrensemble(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
Mdl = fitrensemble(X, Y)
Mdl = fitrensemble(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: 'NumLearningCycles'
parameters.description: Number of boosting rounds / bagged learners (default 100).

parameters.name: 'LearnRate'
parameters.description: Shrinkage for boosting, 0 to 1; smaller needs more cycles.

parameters.name: 'Learners'
parameters.description: A templateTree specification setting depth, leaf size, etc.

tools.name: fitrgp
tools.description: Fit a Gaussian process regression model, a nonparametric Bayesian method that produces both predictions and calibrated uncertainty intervals. The kernel function encodes assumptions about smoothness and length scales. Excellent for small datasets, interpolation and surrogate modelling of expensive simulations.
tools.usage:
gprMdl = fitrgp(Tbl, ResponseVarName)
gprMdl = fitrgp(X, y)
gprMdl = fitrgp(___, Name, Value)

tools.name: anova
tools.description: Produce an analysis-of-variance table for a fitted LinearModel, GeneralizedLinearModel or LinearMixedModel, testing the significance of each term or of the whole model. The 'component' form tests individual terms while 'summary' tests the model as a whole. Use it to decide whether a group of related terms is worth keeping.
tools.usage:
tbl = anova(mdl)
tbl = anova(mdl, anovatype)
tbl = anova(mdl, anovatype, sstype)

tools.name: coefCI
tools.description: Compute confidence intervals for the coefficients of a fitted regression model. The significance level is adjustable and the intervals are based on the t-distribution with the model's residual degrees of freedom. Use it to report coefficient uncertainty alongside point estimates.
tools.usage:
ci = coefCI(mdl)
ci = coefCI(mdl, alpha)

tools.name: plotResiduals
tools.description: Plot the residuals of a fitted model as a histogram, normal probability plot, residual-versus-fitted scatter, or lagged residual plot. These plots reveal non-normality, heteroscedasticity, nonlinearity and autocorrelation. Always look at them before trusting a regression summary.
tools.usage:
plotResiduals(mdl)
plotResiduals(mdl, plottype)
plotResiduals(mdl, plottype, Name, Value)
tools.example:
load carsmall
mdl = fitlm([Weight Horsepower], MPG);
tiledlayout(2,2)
nexttile, plotResiduals(mdl, 'fitted')
nexttile, plotResiduals(mdl, 'probability')
nexttile, plotResiduals(mdl, 'histogram')
nexttile, plotResiduals(mdl, 'lagged')

tools.name: plotDiagnostics
tools.description: Plot regression diagnostics such as leverage, Cook's distance, DFFITS and covariance ratio to find influential observations. Points that stand out have a disproportionate effect on the fitted coefficients. Use it before deciding whether to remove or down-weight suspicious data.
tools.usage:
plotDiagnostics(mdl)
plotDiagnostics(mdl, plottype)
plotDiagnostics(mdl, plottype, Name, Value)
tools.example:
load carsmall
mdl = fitlm([Weight Horsepower], MPG);
plotDiagnostics(mdl, 'cookd')
influential = find(mdl.Diagnostics.CooksDistance > 3*mean(mdl.Diagnostics.CooksDistance))

tools.name: predict
tools.description: Compute predicted responses from a fitted model for new predictor data, with optional confidence or prediction intervals. Every regression and classification model class in the toolbox implements it with the same basic signature. For regression models the second and third outputs give standard deviations and interval bounds.
tools.usage:
ypred = predict(mdl, Xnew)
[ypred, yci] = predict(mdl, Xnew)
[ypred, ysd, yci] = predict(gprMdl, Xnew)
[___] = predict(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: Xnew
parameters.description: New predictor data, as a matrix or a table with matching variable names.

parameters.name: 'Simultaneous'
parameters.description: Logical; simultaneous rather than pointwise bounds.

tools.name: polyconf
tools.description: Evaluate a polynomial fit from polyfit and return confidence or prediction intervals for the fitted values. It uses the structure output of polyfit, so no separate model object is needed. Use it to draw uncertainty bands around a simple polynomial trend line.
tools.usage:
y = polyconf(p, x)
[y, delta] = polyconf(p, x, S)
[y, delta] = polyconf(p, x, S, Name, Value)

parameters.name: p, S
parameters.description: Coefficients and error-estimate structure returned by polyfit.
